question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 36 days while B and C together can do it in 20 days. The efficiency of C is thrice the efficiency of A. B alone can complete two-third of the original work in
solution:
Given:

A and B together can complete a piece of work in 36 days while B and C together can do it in 20 days. 

The efficiency of C is thrice the efficiency of A.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken 

Calculation:

LCM (36, 20) = 180

Let the total work be the LCM of the individual like taken by the group of workers.

Hence, total work = 180 units

Similarly, let A and B do P and Q units work a day respectively.

Thus, C does = 3 × P = 3P units work a day.

According to the question,

(P + Q) × 36 = 180

⇒ P + Q = 180/36

⇒ P + Q = 5

⇒ Q = (5 - P) ....(1)

(Q + 3P) × 20 = 180

⇒ Q + 3P = 180/20

⇒ Q + 3P = 9

⇒ (5 - P) + 3P = 9 (From 1)

⇒ 2P = 4

⇒ P = 2

Now,

Q = 5 - P

⇒ 5 - 2 = 3

Hence, B alone can complete two-third of the original work in

⇒ {180 × {2 over 3}} over 3

⇒ 180 × {2 over 9}

⇒ 40 days

**∴ B alone can complete two-third of the original work in 40 days.**
